title: How Seasonal Reference Choice Changes the Apparent Gains of Chronos Models in Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: On hourly electricity load at 24 and 168 hours ahead, the wins of zero-shot Chronos-Bolt and Chronos-2 shrink when the baseline is a validation-selected seasonal reference rather than weekly persistence (a week ahead, Bolt's clear wins fall from 21 to 14 of 30 cases and its median gain from 17.3% to 11.9%; Chronos-2 from 18 to 15), in a study the authors call exploratory.
why_relevant: Hourly load at exactly our 168-hour horizon with Chronos-2 against simple references, and it is about how the choice of baseline sizes the reported gain; no weather covariates.

title: Calibrated for the Winter, Not for the Cold Snap: a chronological benchmark of 38 extreme-cold events in six U.S. power systems (v2.0.0 of the PJM Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark)
claim: Conformal 90% intervals for day-ahead load that were calibrated on earlier winters cover about 0.64 of hours inside 38 weather-defined extreme-cold events against 0.84 of winter hours (a gap near 20 points, also seen around the operators' own EIA-930 forecasts), in a version 2.0.0 that replaces the design and corrects errors of versions 1.0 to 1.2.
why_relevant: PJM and EIA-930 demand with temperature-driven extremes under a strictly chronological protocol; day-ahead and probabilistic rather than week-ahead point forecasts.

title: Benchmarking Time Series Foundation Models for Load Forecasting Under Covariate Uncertainty
claim: Across three load datasets, Chronos-2 is the most accurate of four foundation models and four trained-from-scratch models when future covariates are exact or accurately forecast, zero-shot and fine-tuned, but it degrades as covariate forecasts get noisier, where TimesNet is more robust.
why_relevant: Directly our oracle-versus-forecast weather question for Chronos-2 on electric load, at short-term horizons and with synthetic covariate noise rather than archived forecasts.

title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model
claim: On ISO New England and ENTSO-E load with weather and calendar covariates, Chronos-2 gains a lot from fine-tuning and is strong at short horizons, but zero-shot it trails task-specific deep models and its error grows faster as the horizon lengthens.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 with temperature covariates on U.S. zonal load, the model and inputs of our primary comparison, against deep models rather than a lag regression.

title: EnergyBench: a live, gate-aligned benchmark of day-ahead forecasts for European power markets
claim: In a live daily benchmark on inputs frozen before the day-ahead gate in six bidding zones, weather covariates cut the error of each of ten foundation models by 37 to 51% over the first 32 days, zero-shot models matched or beat a LightGBM trained on the same covariates, and on load the gap to the grid operators' forecasts was 4 to 6%.
why_relevant: Every model gets the same honestly timed weather forecasts and is compared with and without them, as in our forecast regime; day-ahead on European zones, and 32 days is under our 90-day minimum.

title: Lead-Time-Conditioned Convex Stacked Ensemble for Medium-Term Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: A stacked ensemble of nine base models with convex weights conditioned on lead time is proposed for weekly-ahead daily load and compared against a SARIMA benchmark.
why_relevant: A week-ahead load horizon, the same as ours, but daily resolution, no pretrained model, and the result itself was not read.
query: week-ahead OR medium-term electricity load forecasting

title: Combining Weather Forecast Aggregation and State-Space Models for Adaptive Probabilistic Electricity Load Forecasting
claim: An adaptive GAM with state-space updates that pools weather forecasts from several providers improves point and probabilistic forecasts of French national load over using a single provider, especially in the extreme quantiles.
why_relevant: Electric load driven by real weather forecasts rather than actuals, the heart of our forecast regime, with a regression-family model; national rather than zonal.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments: Results from a 41-day live challenge on the aggregated German transmission-grid load
claim: In a 41-day live day-ahead challenge on German transmission-grid load, a deterministic local pipeline with calendar and weather covariates beat the official ENTSO-E forecast and was competitive with foundation models of more than 100 million parameters such as Chronos-2.
why_relevant: A live, no-lookahead comparison of a simple transparent model with Chronos-2 on hourly grid load with weather; day-ahead, and 41 days is under our 90-day minimum.

title: Physics-Informed Fractional Load Forecasting With Memory-Aware Break Detection for Reserve Scheduling
claim: A day-ahead load model with a fractional temperature kernel for building thermal inertia and joint estimation of breaks and long memory lowers MAPE by 15.7% and 10.3% against the best of ten benchmarks on New England and Mid-Atlantic data.
why_relevant: Temperature-driven load on Mid-Atlantic data, the region of our PJM zones, with a structured temperature response; day-ahead and no pretrained model.

title: Analysis plan for "Donor Choice in Zero-Shot Load-Forecast Transfer: What It Costs, and Why a Pretrained Model Wins"
claim: Across all 272 ordered pairs of 17 Moroccan distribution feeders, no configuration of training a day-ahead model on one feeder and applying it to another beats a seasonal naive forecast, and a zero-shot pretrained model outperforms every configuration measured, under reading rules the authors say were written before each analysis but deposited afterwards.
why_relevant: Zero-shot pretrained forecasting of electric load against simple references with weather-sensitivity tests; feeder level, day-ahead, and the pre-specification is self-declared.

title: Timestral: Mistral's family of time series foundation models (5M to 209M)
claim: Mistral released four zero-shot probabilistic forecasting models from 5M to 209M parameters with known-future covariate support that run on CPUs, and reports the largest as first among zero-shot pretrained models on GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench.
why_relevant: Timestral-209M is already a runnable model in spec.yaml that takes temperature as a known-future input; its weights fall inside our scored window.

title: TimesFM 3.0: natively multivariate zero-shot forecasting with covariates
claim: Google released TimesFM 3.0, a 330M-parameter model pretrained for multivariate forecasting with past-only and known-future covariates, and reports the top rank among foundation models on GIFT-Eval, fev-bench and TIME, with weights under a non-commercial licence.
why_relevant: A covariate-capable successor to the TimesFM 2.5 row we run univariate, so temperature could be passed to it; weights fall inside our scored window and the licence is non-commercial.

title: t0: A Time-Series Foundation Model for Forecasting with Context
claim: The open-weights t0 models (102M and 256M parameters) condition forecasts on past and known-future covariates without retraining, rank third on GIFT-Eval and fev-bench, gain 6.3 points of skill from known-future covariates across 30 tasks, and are among the most accurate on a Victoria electricity-demand benchmark.
why_relevant: A known-future-covariate model that FoundationForecast wraps with native exogenous support, with an electricity-demand result in the paper; weights fall inside our scored window.

title: TimeH2O-v1: H2O.ai's time series foundation model
claim: H2O.ai released TimeH2O-v1, a roughly 0.1B-parameter forecasting model, and reports it first of 32 models on fev-bench by win rate (91.9%, skill score 50.8), ahead of Timestral-209M, t0-gamma, TimesFM-3 and Chronos-2.
why_relevant: Listed in spec.yaml among the FoundationForecast wrappers with native exogenous support, so it could take temperature on our benchmark; weights fall inside our scored window.

title: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation of Time Series Foundation Models for Electrical Load Forecasting
claim: Across four load aggregation levels, pretrained MOIRAI and Chronos-2 beat seasonal naive and XGBoost baselines, and rank-16 LoRA on MOIRAI Large cuts normalized MAE by 7.5% on average while updating about 1% of the parameters, with smaller gains for Chronos-2.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 on electric load from building to country level against simple baselines; about fine-tuning rather than weather inputs.

title: Peak-Aware Short-Term Load Forecasting Across Distribution Grid Aggregation Levels
claim: On open UK and Swiss distribution data, Chronos-2 has the lowest error in high-demand periods at area, substation and feeder level, 20 to 51% below gradient-boosted models, while staying best or near best overall.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 against LightGBM on electric load, two of our leaderboard rows, judged on peaks; distribution level and short-term.

title: Choosing Load Forecasting Methods by Horizon, History and Hour: Reserve and Imbalance Evidence from Four Grids (companion data, protocol and code)
claim: A four-grid study compares load forecasting methods with rolling-origin forecasts from 1 to 180 days ahead and hourly day-ahead forecasts, with combination and selection by horizon and hour and formal accuracy tests, and releases everything needed to reproduce it.
why_relevant: Grid load at horizons that include a week ahead under a rolling-origin protocol like ours; the result itself was not read.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Multi-horizon forecasting of national electricity demand in Türkiye: run records, forecasts and trained models
claim: The archive holds 759 training runs with sealed test forecasts for a study of national electricity demand at several horizons using calendar, holiday and temperature information; the record itself states no headline result.
why_relevant: National electric demand with temperature as an input at several horizons and sealed test forecasts; no result to compare until the paper is read.

title: Machine Learning and Time-Series Foundation Models for Day-Ahead Electricity Forecasting in a University Building
claim: On 57 test days for one university building, TimesFM 3.0 with covariates has the lowest error, about 43% below weekly seasonal naive, without a clear advantage over XGBoost, and its covariates help on holidays but leave overall error almost unchanged.
why_relevant: TimesFM 3.0 with and without weather covariates on hourly electricity against simple baselines; one building, day-ahead, observed weather, and 57 days is under our 90-day minimum.

title: Systematic Evaluation of TabPFN-TS and Chronos-2 for Zero-Shot Heat Load Forecasting in District Heating Networks
claim: For 24-hour hourly heat load in two German district heating networks with ambient temperature as covariate, zero-shot Chronos-2 and TabPFN-TS both beat all trained baselines over a full year, Chronos-2 slightly ahead (CVRMSE 12.48% against 13.07%), under perfect weather with a separate forecast-weather sensitivity check.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 with temperature on an hourly, weather-driven energy load, with both an oracle and a forecast weather setting; heat rather than electricity, day-ahead.

title: The Impact of Covariates on Zero-Shot Building Energy Forecasting
claim: The paper measures how weather and day-type covariates change zero-shot Chronos-2 forecasts of building energy use.
why_relevant: Chronos-2 with and without weather covariates, the contrast behind our primary comparison; building level, and the result itself was not read.

title: Forecasting Daily Household Electricity Demand in a Hot-Arid City: A Comparative Benchmark of Local, Global, Deep and Foundation Models on ESHED-38
claim: Across 38 homes and 48 weekly origins over a 359-day hold-out, zero-shot Chronos-2 is significantly the most accurate one day ahead and statistically tied with TimesFM-2.5, Chronos-Bolt and an ensemble at one week, while recorded weather improved no model, which the authors leave unresolved because the weather record appears to reuse one annual sequence.
why_relevant: Weekly origins and a week-ahead lead with Chronos-2 and TimesFM-2.5, run with and without weather; daily household data rather than hourly zonal load.

title: TRACE-PFNet: Multi-System Electricity Demand Forecasting Source Code and Reproducibility Benchmark
claim: The record releases code and aggregate results for probabilistic day-ahead demand forecasting across Türkiye, Germany-Luxembourg, France, Spain and Poland (15 configurations, 654,120 hourly predictions), studying data-availability constraints and retraining frequency, without stating a headline result.
why_relevant: Hourly system demand under explicit data-availability constraints; day-ahead, no pretrained model named, and no result to compare yet.

title: On the Encoding of Calendar Features in Covariate-Informed Time Series Foundation Models
claim: How calendar covariates are encoded changes the zero-shot accuracy of four covariate-informed foundation models on nine datasets, by up to 9.9% in MASE on ordinary days and far more on holidays, so benchmarks that fix one encoding can distort comparisons.
why_relevant: About how known-future covariates are fed to the models we run, which bears on same-inputs comparisons; calendar features rather than temperature.

title: Covariate Copies Count as Evidence in Time-Series Foundation Models
claim: Covariate-aware foundation models implicitly weight a covariate by how many redundant copies of it are supplied, such as one temperature in two units or several nearby stations, and a training-free bias in variate attention makes forecasts invariant to copies in some architectures.
why_relevant: Bears on how a temperature series should be passed to covariate models so that every model gets the same input; a probe study, not a load backtest.

title: Forecasting Associations, Not Interventions: A Preregistered Causal Audit of Covariate-Aware Time Series Foundation Models
claim: On a preregistered grid with exact counterfactuals, Chronos-2, TiRex-2, TabPFN-TS and TimesFM-2.5 answer what-if covariate queries with the observational association and respond more confounded than a regression, and a few minutes of interventional post-training cuts the gap by up to 83%.
why_relevant: Preregistered evidence on how covariate-aware models, including Chronos-2, use a covariate compared with regression; synthetic and physical systems, not load.

title: CovNovBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Time Series Foundation Models under Covariate Novelty
claim: On 88,476 series where future covariates leave the range seen in the history, none of six covariate-aware foundation models is consistently reliable zero-shot, and point error almost always increases under such covariate novelty.
why_relevant: Speaks to weeks when the temperature forecast leaves the range in the context window, such as cold snaps; treatment covariates on non-energy data.

title: WhatIf-Bench: Benchmarking Intervention-Aware Time Series Forecasting
claim: A benchmark of 37,665 tasks tests whether foundation models and LLMs forecast a target correctly when covariates are set to values that replay past events or are new.
why_relevant: Tests whether covariate-aware models respond to the covariate itself, the mechanism behind a temperature effect; not load, and the result was not read.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Zero-shot time-series foundation models against the Khepri v1.5 baselines for 96-hour carbon-intensity forecasts in nine Nordic bidding zones: a preregistered comparison
claim: In a preregistered comparison, Timestral-5M, Timestral-209M and Chronos-2 without covariates beat unchanged SARIMA and GBM baselines by about 1 to 1.3 MAPE points on 2025 carbon-intensity data, while on a 14-origin post-release hold-out the differences have the same sign but fall inside the preregistered minimum detectable effect.
why_relevant: A timestamped preregistered design with a post-release hold-out for two models we run, at a multi-day hourly horizon; carbon intensity rather than load, univariate.

title: Online Conditional Vine Copulas: Forecasting Electricity Demand
claim: An online, covariate-conditioned vine copula for multivariate distributional forecasts beats unconditional Gaussian and vine copula benchmarks on net demand in five regions of Great Britain, at much lower cost than batch re-estimation.
why_relevant: Regional electricity demand with covariates and a sequential, no-lookahead update; probabilistic and multivariate, no pretrained model.

title: Medium-Term Multi-Resolution Electric Load Forecasting using Economic Data and Foundation Model
claim: For French load 1 to 48 months ahead at monthly and daily resolution, a tabular foundation model with selected economic covariates improves forecast skill by about 20% over 2015 to 2025, holding MAPE near 4% monthly and 5% daily.
why_relevant: A pretrained model with covariates, weather among them, on electric load; horizons of months to years rather than a week.

title: Hybrid deep learning models for medium-term electricity load forecasting
claim: A hybrid deep learning model is proposed for electricity demand weeks to months ahead without exogenous data.
why_relevant: A load horizon that includes ours, but univariate and trained from scratch; the result itself was not read.
query: week-ahead OR medium-term electricity load forecasting

title: A survey and benchmark for household electricity forecasting: From statistical to foundation models
claim: The paper reviews and benchmarks 30 models, from statistical methods to zero-shot foundation models, on household load, photovoltaic generation and battery operation in one framework with public code.
why_relevant: Foundation models against classical baselines on electricity load; household level, and the ranking itself was not read.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Ranking reliability in building level day ahead load forecasting: analysis code
claim: The code measures how the length of the evaluation window and the number of compared forecasters change the reliability of model rankings, with sixteen forecasters including pretrained models under a 10-origin competition protocol and a 238-origin rolling protocol on the same data.
why_relevant: About how many origins a load leaderboard needs before its order can be trusted, which applies to our 52 scored weeks; building level, and the record states the design, not a result.

title: What a Forecasting Leaderboard Can Establish: Resolution Reporting for Zero-Shot Time-Series Models
claim: A tool that computes the smallest difference a leaderboard can detect finds that GIFT-Eval, fev-bench, Chronos Benchmark II and TIME cannot separate their top entries (resolution 3.6 to 19 times the gap between neighbours), and that shortening the history raised the error of three of four open models, two of them by 15%.
why_relevant: Qualifies the leaderboard ranks that the model releases in this scan cite as evidence, and flags context length as an unrecorded input; not a load result.

title: The Hidden Look-Ahead: Point-in-Time Leakage in Electricity Market Data
claim: Selecting the latest weather run issued before a GB auction gate picks a run not yet published at the gate on more than 99% of days for six of ten weather-model configurations, and the apparent accuracy effect of that leak ranges from -9% to +24%, so it must be measured rather than assumed.
why_relevant: A direct check on our no-lookahead rule for the forecast weather regime: issue time is not availability time; about market data and prices, not a load model.

title: OpenSTEF 4.0: modular short-term energy forecasting with a foundation-model forecaster and a backtesting framework
claim: LF Energy announced OpenSTEF 4.0, a modular rewrite of the grid operators' short-term forecasting library that adds a foundation-model forecaster and a backtesting framework.
why_relevant: An operator-grade load forecasting library with weather inputs and its own backtest harness; a feature announcement with no accuracy claim.

title: ci-proto: Continuous Intelligence's pretrained forecasting model with very long context
claim: Continuous Intelligence released ci-proto, a 167M-parameter pretrained forecasting model that reads more than two million steps of history, accepts past and known-future covariates, runs on CPU or GPU, and is claimed to lead fev-bench.
why_relevant: A new open model that takes known-future covariates such as temperature and runs on CPU; it has no FoundationForecast wrapper in spec.yaml and its weights fall at the very end of our scored window.

title: Tabby: An Open Pretraining Recipe for Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Huawei released Tabby, a 145M-parameter encoder-only forecasting model with contexts up to 8,192 steps and a fully open training recipe, reporting competitive zero-shot results on GIFT-Eval and the TIME benchmark.
why_relevant: Listed in spec.yaml among the FoundationForecast wrappers we can run univariate; no covariates and no load result.

title: Timer-M1: A Multivariate Time Series Foundation Model via Learning Primitives
claim: Timer-M1 is a pretrained multivariate model with target, past-only and known-future covariate roles that the authors report first on FEV and TIME and second on GIFT-Eval among recent foundation models.
why_relevant: A known-future-covariate model that could in principle take temperature; no wrapper in spec.yaml, and public weights were not confirmed in this scan.

title: TabPFN-3.5: Technical Report
claim: Prior Labs released TabPFN-3.5, a tabular foundation model that it reports as state of the art on TabArena and as stronger than its predecessor in the time-series forecasting harness, which tabpfn-time-series uses by default from version 1.3.0.
why_relevant: TabPFN-TS takes weather as ordinary feature columns and is wrapped by FoundationForecast, so the new base model changes a row we could run; the report gives no load result.

title: Granite Timeseries Ensemble r1: one recipe over four IBM Granite forecasting models
claim: IBM released an ensemble recipe that combines four Granite time-series architectures and returns median and quantile forecasts with no retraining and no fitted ensemble weights.
why_relevant: An open pretrained forecaster from a family FoundationForecast wraps (FlowState, PatchTSTFM); no load or covariate claim was seen.

title: SAP-RPT-TS: SAP's time series foundation model
claim: SAP announced SAP-RPT-TS, a roughly 28M-parameter zero-shot forecasting model, and reports the lowest MASE (about 1.41) and scaled quantile loss among the models in its fev-bench chart and first-tier results on GIFT-Eval.
why_relevant: A new pretrained forecasting model from a vendor; no load or covariate claim, and public weights were not confirmed.

title: ElecLoad: Adaptive Electricity Load Forecasting Guided by Multiple Events
claim: A trained context-aware agent that reads notices, weather alerts and event schedules and splits the forecast horizon by changes in event effects is reported as state of the art in most scenarios on several electricity load datasets.
why_relevant: Electric load with weather-related context; textual events rather than a temperature series, and no fixed week-ahead protocol.

title: From Shared Demand Patterns to Local Uncertainty: Probabilistic Load Forecasting by Mixing Compact Adaptations
claim: A shared model with a small bank of low-dimensional adaptations mixed per customer improves point and probabilistic accuracy over statistical, neural and pretrained baselines on 590 SMART-DS load profiles at low storage and inference cost.
why_relevant: Electric load with pretrained time-series baselines in the comparison; customer and transformer level on synthetic profiles.

title: Adaptive Residual Modeling for Scenario Learning in Probabilistic Load Forecasting
claim: A two-stage feeder-level scenario model that calibrates extreme quantiles separately reaches a 0.99-quantile pinball loss 30 to 85% below three baselines on the FeederBW dataset with a 1.05% exceedance rate against a nominal 1%.
why_relevant: Multi-horizon electric load with an environmental-response component; feeder level and about tail quantiles, no pretrained model.

title: Probabilistic electrical power demand forecasting with uncertainty quantification
claim: Across the power-consumption zones studied, NGBoost gives lower MAE and RMSE and better-calibrated intervals than Bayesian, Monte Carlo dropout and Gaussian-process models.
why_relevant: Zonal electricity consumption with a gradient-boosting family model; horizon, data and weather inputs are not stated in the abstract.

title: Evaluating Accuracy and Probabilistic Reliability of Zero-Shot Time Series Foundation Models
claim: Six zero-shot foundation models beat statistical and supervised baselines on energy, traffic and finance datasets but trade point accuracy against calibration, with patch-based transformers miscalibrated at long horizons.
why_relevant: Zero-shot models on energy data across horizons; no covariates, and the models and horizons are not named in the abstract.

title: Foundation or Formula? A Simulation-Based Comparison of Google's TimesFM-3 and Classical Time-Series Models
claim: On 7,200 simulated series under a pre-registered protocol with a 12-step horizon, TimesFM-3 is never worse than 1.31 times the best method while every classical method fails badly somewhere, yet automatic ARIMA is 21 to 24% more accurate on seasonal data with four or more cycles and the robustness holds only at short horizons.
why_relevant: A pre-registered foundation-model-against-simple-baseline comparison on data the model cannot have seen; simulated series, not load, no covariates.

title: A Later Test Set Is Not a New Domain: Pretraining Familiarity Survives a Contamination-Free Hold-Out
claim: On data published after every tested model's release, pretrained forecasters win 5 of 7 groups, and what tracks their advantage is how familiar the domain is from the pretraining corpus rather than seasonality or spectral entropy.
why_relevant: Bears on our weeks-after-weights label: a post-release window removes memorised windows but not domain familiarity; not a load result.

title: When Do Time Series Foundation Models Help Forecast Wind Energy Droughts? A Preregistered Evaluation (code and results)
claim: A preregistered study evaluates Chronos-2, TimesFM 2.5 and Moirai-2 with weather-model covariates against climatology, model output statistics, quantile regression and a recurrent network for probabilistic forecasts of cumulative wind energy deficit in 16 regions.
why_relevant: A preregistered test of two models we run with forecast weather as covariates on an energy series; wind deficit rather than load, and the result was not read.

title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage: Can they replace market-specific forecasting models?
claim: Over 2021 to 2025 in Germany, Poland and Spain, only the TabPFN variants among nine zero-shot foundation models consistently beat two market-specific price forecasting benchmarks, and that statistical lead does not carry over to every battery trading strategy.
why_relevant: A five-year zero-shot comparison with strong domain baselines on an hourly energy series that uses load forecasts as inputs; prices, not load.

title: Timestral and t0-gamma: Do the Leaderboard Leaders Win on Real Prices?
claim: A practitioner tests whether Timestral and t0-gamma, the leaderboard leaders, also win on a year of German day-ahead electricity prices against Chronos-2, TimesFM-3 and LightGBM.
why_relevant: A claimed-versus-measured check of two new releases on an hourly energy series over a year; prices rather than load, and the outcome was not read.
query: TimesFM OR Chronos-2 OR Timestral OR TabPFN-TS electricity load

title: Can Foundation Models Beat a Tuned LightGBM on Electricity Prices?
claim: On seven days of German day-ahead prices from 2017 with load and renewables forecasts as covariates, zero-shot foundation models rank around a tuned LightGBM, and the order among them is decided by a single day.
why_relevant: Zero-shot models with known-future covariates against LightGBM on an hourly energy series; prices, and a seven-day window far under our 90-day minimum.
query: electricity load forecasting foundation model benchmark

title: Forecasting energy consumption with AI: Timestral on a steel plant
claim: A company reports that Timestral-28M, forecasting a steel plant's consumption a day ahead over one December month, had roughly a quarter less error than repeating the previous week's profile.
why_relevant: A Timestral model on electricity consumption against a weekly-persistence reference; one industrial site, one month, day-ahead.

title: U.S. utility load forecasts filed on FERC Form 714, 2006-2025: forecast errors, weather-normalized outcomes, prediction intervals and capacity decision rules (code and data)
claim: The record evaluates the summer-peak, winter-peak and energy forecasts that U.S. planning areas filed for 2006 to 2025 against weather-normalized outcomes (13,657 forecast-outcome pairs) and builds prediction intervals from past errors, including a look at PJM's own forecasts.
why_relevant: Measured errors of filed U.S. load forecasts, PJM among them, with weather normalization; planning horizons of years rather than a week, and no model to run.
